core_obligations: Invoke the right-acyclicity criterion and reduce to two conditions: embeddability into the class, which follows from injective implies flasque, and the exactness of the section functors on short exact sequences with flasque first two terms (proof lines 1919-1931).

For the second condition, let s be a section of H over an open U and consider the partially ordered set T of pairs (V, t) with V contained in U and t a section of G over V mapping to s; show every totally ordered subset has an upper bound by the sheaf condition and choose a maximal element by Zorn (proof lines 1932-1944).

Show the maximal (V, t) has V = U: for x in U pick a local lift t' over a neighbourhood W, use flasqueness of F to modify t' so that t and t' agree on W cap V, glue by the sheaf condition of G, and contradict maximality unless V contains x (proof lines 1945-1957).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the acyclicity criterion (proof lines 1919-1931).
Lift sections by a maximality argument (proof lines 1932-1944).
Extend the maximal lift one point at a time using flasqueness of the subsheaf (proof lines 1945-1957).
difficulty_reason: For a ringed space (X, O_X) the lemma asserts that any flasque O_X-module is acyclic for R Gamma(X, -) and for R Gamma(U, -) for every open U (statement lines 1912-1917). The proof invokes the general criterion that a class of objects is right acyclic for a functor once every object embeds into one of them and the class is closed under quotients in short exact sequences whose sections stay exact, and it verifies those two conditions directly (proof lines 1919-1931). The verification is the content: given a short exact sequence with F and G flasque and a section s of H over an open U, the author lifts s by a Zorn argument on the partially ordered set of pairs (V, t) with t mapping to s over V, and shows a maximal element must have V = U; the extension step uses flasqueness of F to correct the difference of two local lifts and then the sheaf condition of G to glue (proof lines 1932-1957). The claim is H2: one general criterion plus a self-contained Zorn and gluing argument, with no step left to the reader.
